title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages. Write Ss = Δ^ = simplicial sets. An 'additive contravariant invariant' is a functor F : Ss^op → A that turns colimits of simplicial sets into limits (equivalently, F is determined by its values on the Δ^n). Here A is an additive category with all small limits, or dually with colimits. Such F correspond to (co)simplicial objects K_* of A. Via Dold–Kan / Dold–Puppe (normalized complex ND., inverse DP_*), they also correspond to complexes K.. Concretely, F(X_*) = Hom_*(C_*(X_*), K_*) = Hom.(C.(X_*), K.).

The universal such object is the simplicial abelian group n ↦ Z[Δ^n], viewed in (Ab_*)^op. 'Operations' on these invariants are natural constructions compatible with every limit-preserving functor A → A'. By a Yoneda / Lawvere-theory argument they are given by objects L_* ∈ Ab_*, or L. ∈ Ab.: Ω(F) = Hom_*(L_*, K_*). Dually, covariant invariants G(X_*) = C_*(X_*) ⊗_* K^* have operations Ω(G) = L_* ⊗_* K^*.

This page has two remarks.

(a) The same object L_* (equivalently L.) represents operations on both contravariant and covariant additive invariants. This was clear a priori, since passing from A to B = A^op exchanges the two cases. The difference is that L acts contravariantly in the first case and covariantly in the second (Hom versus ⊗).

(b) The initial problem, 'determine all possible operations on additive invariants of this type', is solved quasi-tautologically. The answer is Ab_*, equivalently Ab. by Dold–Kan, or its opposite. The answer is so tautological because very special value categories were allowed: ones in which all lim (or all colim) can be formed.

Grothendieck then proposes a refinement. Fix a set L of index categories and require of the value categories only limits of type L (or colimits of type L). Then both the category of operations and the 'universal' category get smaller. Precisely, let F_0 : Δ^op → B_0 = (Ab_*)^op be the universal simplicial object, the one represented by the Z[Δ^n]. The category of operations is then the full subcategory U_L of B_0 generated by the F_0(n) under L-limits. Equivalently, it is the full subcategory of Ab_* generated by the C_*(Δ^n) under L-colimits.

The next page treats the case L = ∅: one gets the full additive subcategory of Ab_* generated by finite direct sums of the Z[Δ^n]. It also announces that everything holds for an arbitrary small category in place of Δ, and in a non-additive context. Grothendieck says these 'general principles' are not detailed here.

The purpose is to fix a framework for which natural operations exist on cochains and cohomology-type invariants of simplicial sets. This prepares the divided-power de Rham / Dold–Puppe material of the 1976 lecture.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. The 'general principles' (free completion of the category of representables under a class L of limits) are asserted, not proved, as Grothendieck himself notes.

Size and existence issues are not addressed: requiring all small limits in an additive category, and the variance bookkeeping between (Ab_*)^op and (Ab^*_*)^op, are glossed. The latter is easy to garble.

ideas.what: Additive limit-preserving invariants of simplicial sets are classified by (co)simplicial objects, or by complexes via Dold–Kan; the universal one is Z[Δ^•] in Ab_* or its opposite.
ideas.modern_name: Free (additive) cocompletion of Z[Δ]; Ab_* as additive presheaves on Δ; Kan extension along Yoneda
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kan (1958), Dold–Kan; free cocompletion: SGA4 I (Grothendieck–Verdier), Kelly
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. I (presheaf categories as free cocompletions), in general form

ideas.what: Natural operations on such invariants are represented by objects of Ab_* (or Ab.), acting by Hom (contravariant case) or ⊗ (covariant case); the same representing object serves both variances via A ↦ A^op.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic theory / Lawvere theory of (co)simplicial objects in additive categories; co-operations represented by Yoneda

ideas.what: Restricting the value categories to have only limits of a prescribed class L makes the category of operations the closure U_L of the representables under L-(co)limits inside Ab_*; for L = ∅ this is the additive closure (finite sums of Z[Δ^n]).
ideas.modern_name: Free L-cocompletion / closure of representables under a class of colimits; doctrine of L-complete categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory (1982) ch. 5; Albert–Kelly (1988); Gabriel–Ulmer (1971) for finite limits

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes classifying cochain-level operations relative to a chosen class L of (co)limits, so that operations form U_L ⊂ Ab_*. He announces a non-additive version and one for arbitrary small categories in place of Δ, both left undetailed. The general categorical statement is now standard (Kelly, Albert–Kelly). Its explicit use as a tool for organizing operations on cochains and divided-power / de Rham-type constructions in this 1976 setting is not something I know to have been developed from these notes.
missed.quote: on trouve des catégories correspondantes d'opérations (ou constructions) sur invariants plus petites en même temps qu'on trouve des cat. "universelles" plus petites
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This resembles current practice in derived algebraic geometry, where operations on cochains are classified via functors on lattices or polynomial / Dold–Puppe-type categories, and where derived de Rham and divided powers are handled by restricting to finite-coproduct or sifted-colimit structure. The parallel is of historical interest, not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a methodological remark: a Yoneda / free-completion classification of operations, plus the observation that restricting the allowed limit class L shrinks the universal category to the L-closure of representables. This anticipates Kelly-style free L-cocompletions by a few years in an applied setting, but the content is categorical folklore and Grothendieck himself calls it quasi-tautological.
transcription_corrections: The functor in 'F_0 : A^0 → B_0' is written 'Δ° → B_0' in the image: F_0 is the universal simplicial object Δ^op → B_0.
'Ab' in 'deux catégories, Ab_* et Ab' should be 'Ab.' (chain complexes), the Dold–Kan partner of Ab_*.
'(Ab^{**})^0' is more plausibly '(Ab^*_*)^°', i.e. (Ab_*)^* opposite, as on the next page.
Read '(que je n'ai pas détaillés)' and 'c'était clair a priori à cause du passage de A à B par catégorie opposée'.
'vérifier les lim' is likely 'exiger les lim'.
The last lines read: 'et correspond dans la sous-catégorie pleine de Ab_* engendrée par les colim de type L'.
The marginal 'U_L' labels the full subcategory of B_0 = (Ab_*)^° generated by F_0 under lim of type L.
